A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STFlow, with matching authors, core formulation and retained N-body/MD17 experiments. The complete text, equations, tables, figures and technical appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original STFlow results on synthetic N-body systems, MD17 and ETH-UCY, alongside ablations, density analyses and inference-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for STFlow and its Transformer variant on N-body systems, MD17 and NBA trajectories, including ablations and computational scaling measurements.

M1.justification: v2 introduces STFlow-Transformer, replacing the UNet temporal component with a Transformer and evaluating this architectural alternative throughout the benchmarks. The coupled random-walk prior, flow-matching loss and spatial message-passing foundation remain.

E1.justification: The three synthetic N-body systems and eight MD17 molecules remain, but all five ETH-UCY pedestrian scenes are replaced by SportVU NBA player-and-ball forecasting, including Rebound and Score scenarios. This changes the represented population and interaction requirements.

E2.justification: N-body and MD17 comparisons remove SVAE and add LaM-SLidE while retaining TFN, SE(3)-Tr, EGNN, EqMotion and GeoTDM. The replacement human-trajectory experiments introduce evaluated comparisons with GroupNet, LED and MoFlow; Trajectron++ and SVAE participate in NBA setup 1.

E3.justification: Default Euler inference changes from 50 to 5 evaluations, MD17 training increases from 300 to 400 epochs, and augmentation and scheduler settings change. New protocols cover Transformer configurations, two NBA evaluation setups and Aspirin scaling measurements over 150–4000 frames. Skewed training-time sampling was already documented for most experiments in v1 Table 6; Charged's reported distribution changes from uniform to square-root-uniform.

E4.justification: Gravity/Ethanol ablations become Gravity-only tests covering both temporal architectures, with new temporal-layer removal and transport-cost measurements. The Gaussian-at-last-position control becomes a Gaussian-velocity random walk, and the no-update control changes from freezing positions and edges to freezing edges. v2 adds scaling and prior-density comparisons but removes the Euler/RK4 sampling study and pedestrian case studies.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix A.5, Tables 8–9, reports standard deviations for N-body and MD17 results. v2 removes these uncertainty tables without replacement, while retaining means over five inference runs per test sample.

E6.justification: Reported Gravity ADE/FDE changes from 0.115/0.245 to 0.107/0.231, while Spring changes from 0.0002/0.0004 to 0.0004/0.0008. These accompany revised training or inference settings and do not establish controlled version-to-version gains or losses. MD17 values also change; Transformer, NBA and scaling results are added, while ETH-UCY results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.3 adds a computational-complexity derivation from O(L(|E|d^2 + NTd^2)) to O(LNTd^2), invoking distance-threshold connectivity. The core coupling, random-walk and EGCL mathematics remain substantially unchanged; no corresponding complexity derivation appears in v1.

C1.justification: The central claim that informed coupling improves trajectory simulation remains. v2 adds explicit core claims of time-shift equivariance and linear scaling in both particle count and trajectory length, and makes five-evaluation simulation part of its concluding contribution statement.

C2.justification: The prior rationale remains, but density interpretation shifts from matching rare-event frequencies to correcting a unimodal prior into multimodal dynamics. v2 adds a prior diversity/fidelity trade-off and removes pedestrian-overfitting discussion. Its architecture-ablation prose also reverses spatial and temporal roles relative to Table 5.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents frame-index embeddings, an empty UNet attention-resolution setting, Transformer configurations and NBA team/ball features. Appendix A.4 replaces the A100 specification and per-dataset runtime table with several GPU types, runtime ranges and approximately 750 total GPU hours. These update reproducibility information without establishing that every newly disclosed detail represents an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around coupling, symmetry and scalability, explicitly contrasting STFlow with LaM-SLidE and MoFlow in related work and a new property table. It adds references including rectified flow, MotionDiffuser, GroupNet, FLUX.1 Kontext and neural operators, while removing much of v1's pedestrian and PDE-diffusion background.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, architecture explanation and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Temporal convolution becomes temporal mixing, the sampling-efficiency section is replaced by scaling, the human-trajectory narrative is reorganized, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two columns, with new property and scaling displays and redesigned density and ablation presentations. Pedestrian and uncertainty displays are removed. The architecture diagram is retained as v2 Figure 1, and the Charged trajectory panel moves from v1 Figure 3 to v2 Appendix Figure 8.

improvement.justification: Newer comparator coverage and direct transport-cost, temporal-layer and scaling analyses strengthen empirical assessment. However, v2 removes uncertainty reporting, and its new claims of time-shift equivariance and linear scaling in particle count are not reconciled with frame-index embeddings, fully connected benchmark graphs, or a scaling study that fixes N=21. These substantive gains and unresolved weaknesses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
